chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Isḥaq, who said:
I asked Abu Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him) about the working camels; is there zakāt upon them? He said, 'Yes, there is zakāt upon them.'

key_terms.أَبُو إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Abu Ibrāhīm (Imam al-Ṣādiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.الإِبِلِ الْعَامِلِ: working camels (livestock kept for labor or profit)

ai.seo_question: Is zakat obligatory on working camels in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that camels designated as 'working' (al-ibl al-amil) are subject to zakāt, resolving potential ambiguity regarding whether their utility for labor exempts them from this financial obligation. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the primary function of the livestock—whether for profit, labor, or grazing—determines its zakāt liability, reflecting the practical application of divine law to economic activities. The confirmation by the Imam highlights the continuity of prophetic economic principles within the Imami tradition, ensuring that assets generating value remain accountable to the purifying duty of zakāt.
